findings.summary: The drain picks the slot-wait outcome by checking whether the error text starts with BUILD_SLOT_WAIT, when it could check the error's type.
findings.evidence: The drain builds run.reason as format!("{error:#}") (drain.rs 3707). With {:#}, any context added on the way out of go is printed before the SlotWait text, so starts_with(BUILD_SLOT_WAIT) would fail and the job would be labelled `environment: low disk` again. BUDGET_SHORT avoids this: the drain checks the error's type first and then writes the prefix itself (3699-3705). Fix: In the Err arm, use error.downcast_ref::<SlotWait>() and either carry the hold kind on Run or prefix the reason with BUILD_SLOT_WAIT, as is done for BudgetShort. Then select the outcome from that, not from the raw error text.

findings.summary: The new stop reason is left to the generic OtherEnvironment variant, but StopCause's own doc says each new kind of environment stop is added there.
findings.evidence: disk.rs 366: 'A new kind of environment stop is now added here once.' LowDisk, CheckTimeout, ProducerAuth and UsageLimit each have a variant. Fix: Add StopCause::BuildSlotWait (matched by the BUILD_SLOT_WAIT prefix) and test it, or say in the plan why OtherEnvironment is enough.

findings.summary: Baseline checks and the 'fails without' reruns still compile and test without a slot, so with max_in_flight > 1 they can run beside a check that holds the only slot.
findings.evidence: Design section 4 lists 'SnapExec::exec ... (local checks and reruns)' as class 2. The plan says demonstration_runs and baseline_checks call run_check directly and leaves them unwrapped. Fix: Keep the open question, but state the gap plainly in the design-note update and the CHANGELOG entry: the limit covers the checks stage only, and baseline runs and reruns are not limited yet. That way the 'build wait' figure is not read as covering all local builds.
findings.location: Dependents entry 'RefuseExec, demonstration_runs and baseline_checks' / Open questions

findings.summary: Throughput.build_wait should be left out of status JSON when it is None, and the plan should say the line appears after any locally run check.
findings.evidence: status_snapshot.rs 95-96 compares the throughput JSON. Step 6 sets queued_s = Some(..) on every local check, even an uncontended one, so 'only when some check has queued_s' means the line shows up as soon as any job runs a local check after this lands. Fix: Put #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] on build_wait. In the design note, say the line also counts uncontended waits, which are near zero.

summary: Round 2. The plan covers step 3 of the design, and the code bears out what it says. Read and Grep confirmed: SnapExec::exec does stop check, then the disk gate once, then run_check, then restore_to (run/checks.rs 31-60). The LowDisk downcast is at run/mod.rs 1609. hold_for_disk is in close.rs 177. read_hold is used only at status.rs 1709 and run/mod.rs 402. The drain's held classification (drain.rs 3711) and outcome choice (1616-1621) are where the plan says. check_seam is thread-local (run/mod.rs 1203). A catch_unwind precedent exists (run/tests.rs 2554). FreeSpace is fn(&Path), so the re-gate test's file trick works. LowDisk has no deny_unknown_fields, but each hold type has required fields the other lacks, so neither marker reads as the other. The dependents list matches the readers found by grep, and no PipelineConfig struct literal or concurrent-check test is missed. Each demonstration uses real lock files, threads or child processes through production entry points, and would fail without the behavior. Athena's ten scope findings are justified: the compiler forces queued_s into those files, and the drain change stops slot waits being reported as low disk. All remaining findings are minor: the drain matches a message prefix where it could check the error type; StopCause gets no variant of its own; baseline checks and reruns are not wrapped; and status JSON and output need small care.
